author: vladimir_ea
content:
In gloas attestations (on the beacon block and the PTC attestations) are given 3 seconds to propagate through the network (if i understand correctly), this is not the case for the execution payload. 

- builder must send payload to arrive at PTC members BY the 6s mark
- aggregators include attestations received UP TO the 6s mark

if a block builder is to observe attestations AND ensure the execution payload arrives at PTC members by the 6s mark, then no block builder, however well connected, can ever observe the same attestations as the aggregators, since it has to sacrifice some portion of the attestation propagation window to ensure that the payload propagates.

So the builder is by design forced to operate with uncertainty: it cannot form the same view of attestations as an aggregator so can only ever have a probabilistic view of whether or not a beacon block will be accepted - and so a builder may form a different view from attestation aggregators simply because, for example, many attestations are slow to propagate. 

if there is such a diverge of views, either the builder does not release the payload but has to pay anyway because the aggregators, with the benefit of extra time, think that it should have - or it does release the payload but it is not included and users transactions can be unbundled / exploited etc. So either way there is increased jeopardy for builders compared to now. 

is this an unintended consequence of the design? or something that is intended? the squeeze on payload propagation time seems out of step with the rest of the design.

author: potuz
content:
attestations have about 9 seconds to propagate, depending on peering, they have about 3 seconds if they require being seen by an aggregator, and then aggregates have about 6 seconds to propagate. 

PTC attestations have 3 seconds. 

The builder can form a subset of the view of aggregators, if the builder has seen 40% of the attestations then it's safe they can rebroadcast those attestations themselves (their node will do this automatically). And we're p99 in well under 1 second on mainnet for 40% of the committee.

author: potuz
content: In addition the builder can never be same-slot-unbundled, which, of course is not remotely comparable with not being unbundled, but it is a better situation than in pre-Gloas where unbundling can replay transactions with the same slot context.
